title: Hammersmith Odeon, London ’75
note: Columbia had covered the theatre in posters announcing that London was finally ready for Bruce Springsteen, and he was so mortified by the hype that he reportedly tore some of them down before the show. What follows is a tense, coiled first night in Europe: a 26-year-old trying to outrun his own press. The film sat in the vault for thirty years before it came out in 2005.

title: Houston ’78 Bootleg: House Cut
note: The 1978 tour is where the marathon E Street show was born, and this is its most complete record on video. A legal fight with his former manager had kept Bruce out of the studio for about a year, and these shows have a nothing-to-lose edge. It was filmed by the arena’s own screen cameras, so the picture is rough, but the performance is the point.
caveat: Officially streams only on Apple Music, as a video album you play song by song.

title: The Legendary 1979 No Nukes Concerts
note: Filmed at Madison Square Garden in September 1979 for the MUSE anti-nuclear benefits, just before his 30th birthday and between Darkness and The River. Only a handful of songs made the original No Nukes film; the full restored set waited until 2021. It’s the best-looking footage of the young E Street Band in full flight.
caveat: Free on PBS for now. It may later need PBS Passport.
also: Rent or buy on Amazon, Apple and Fandango at Home

title: The River Tour, Tempe 1980
note: Filmed the night after the 1980 presidential election, which Bruce acknowledged from the stage before tearing into the set. The River tour is where the shows grew into two-set, three-hour epics that balance bar-band party songs with the album’s quieter, more adult ballads. Restored for The Ties That Bind box in 2015.
caveat: Officially streams only on Apple Music, as a video album you play song by song.

title: In Concert / MTV Plugged
note: Bruce let the E Street Band go in 1989 and toured Human Touch and Lucky Town with a new group, still often called the ‘Other Band’. This was meant to be an MTV Unplugged; after one acoustic song he plugged in. Long seen as his most divisive era, it has aged better than its reputation.

title: Blood Brothers
note: In early 1995 Bruce called the E Street Band back into the studio to record new songs for his Greatest Hits, their first real work together in years. The film catches the awkward, affectionate process of a band rediscovering itself, years before the full reunion tour. It’s patient, intimate and quietly moving.

title: Live in New York City
note: The final shows of the 1999–2000 reunion tour, from a ten-night stand at Madison Square Garden. It’s the E Street Band at full strength again after more than a decade apart. It also features ‘American Skin (41 Shots)’, written after the police killing of Amadou Diallo, which drew fierce criticism from police unions.

title: Live in Barcelona
note: The Rising was Bruce’s answer to September 11, and his first studio album with the full E Street Band since Born in the U.S.A. Here those songs of grief and resilience meet one of his most passionate audiences. Watch it after New York City to hear how much heavier the band sounds two years on.

title: VH1 Storytellers
note: Recorded in the Devils & Dust period, this is Bruce as a close reader of his own songs, playing them alone and taking them apart between verses. In hindsight it’s a clear sketch for Springsteen on Broadway: the humour, the self-deprecation, and the gap between the man and the characters he writes.
caveat: On Tubi it is listed simply as ‘Bruce Springsteen (2005)’. Tubi is US-only.

title: Wings for Wheels: The Making of Born to Run
note: After two acclaimed but slow-selling records, Born to Run was a make-or-break album, and Bruce spent months on the title track alone chasing a wall-of-sound grandeur. The film shows how close the album came to collapsing under his perfectionism. It closes with rare live footage from 1973.
also: Rent or buy on Apple and Fandango at Home

title: New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival
note: Eight months after Hurricane Katrina, Bruce brought his big Seeger Sessions folk band to the first Jazz Fest after the storm. Old protest and folk songs suddenly sounded like news, and he added new verses to ‘How Can a Poor Man Stand Such Times and Live?’ aimed at the city’s situation. Many fans count it among his great one-off performances.

title: Live in Dublin
note: The Seeger Sessions tour at its loosest, in a city where Irish folk roots and American hootenanny meet. Bruce reworks some of his own songs in the same brass-and-fiddle spirit. Pure joy, and a reminder of how deeply he loves the American songbook he came out of.

title: Darkness on the Edge of Town, Asbury Park
note: For The Promise box set, the E Street Band played the whole Darkness album, in order, in an empty Paramount Theatre on the Asbury Park boardwalk. With no crowd, the songs come across as the stark, grown-up statement they were in 1978. A natural companion to The Promise.
caveat: Officially streams only on Apple Music, as a video album you play song by song.

title: London Calling: Live in Hyde Park
note: It opens with The Clash’s ‘London Calling’ and runs from late-afternoon sun into darkness. It’s one of the last full shows filmed with Clarence Clemons, who died in 2011, and a fine portrait of the late-2000s E Street Band at stadium scale.

title: The Promise: The Making of Darkness on the Edge of Town
note: The legal dispute with his former manager kept Bruce out of the studio for about a year. What came after was Darkness, leaner and angrier than Born to Run. Built from home-movie footage of the sessions, the film shows him shelving dozens of strong songs to protect the album’s mood. This edition also includes a 2010 performance filmed in Asbury Park.

title: Springsteen & I
note: Less a portrait of Bruce than of what he means to people, made from videos sent in by fans around the world. It’s sentimental by design. Anyone who has felt personally addressed by a Springsteen song will recognise themselves in it.

title: Born in the U.S.A. Live: London 2013
note: The whole Born in the U.S.A. album, in order, from Hyde Park. Heard in sequence, the record is much darker than its stadium reputation: songs about veterans, dead-end jobs and getting out of town. Bruce spent years correcting the misreading of that record.
caveat: Only the album portion of the show. Officially on Apple Music only.

title: Bruce Springsteen: In His Own Words
note: A BBC documentary that lets Bruce tell his own story through interviews from across the decades. A gentle overview, and a good refresher on the whole arc from Freehold onward before you dive into the deeper cuts.
also: Streaming on BritBox and BBC Select via Apple TV

title: Springsteen on Broadway
note: A one-man show drawn from his 2016 memoir Born to Run, which played 236 nights at the Walter Kerr Theatre. He opens by joking that he’s never held an honest job, a disarming start to an evening about memory, his father, and the myths rock and roll makes. Perhaps the closest thing to Bruce talking to you directly.

title: Western Stars
note: His lush, orchestral album of Western Americana, inspired by the Southern California pop of the late ’60s and early ’70s, performed with a band and strings in his century-old barn. Spoken interludes about love, restlessness and settling down tie it together. Co-directed by Bruce, it’s one of his most reflective late works.
also: Rent or buy on Amazon, Apple and Fandango at Home

title: Asbury Park: Riot, Redemption, Rock & Roll
note: Not really a Bruce film, but the story of the town that shaped him: the 1970 riots that devastated Asbury Park’s West Side, the club scene that grew up anyway, and the city’s slow revival. Essential context for the boardwalk mythology of his first records.
also: Rent or buy on Amazon and Apple

title: Letter to You
note: The album was recorded live with the E Street Band in his home studio in a matter of days, and it’s a meditation on mortality, prompted partly by the death of George Theiss, his bandmate in his first group, the Castiles. Shot in black and white, the film becomes an elegy for Clarence Clemons, Danny Federici and the others he’s lost, and a celebration of those still in the room.
also: Rent or buy on Amazon, Apple and Fandango at Home

title: Road Diary
note: Follows the 2023 world tour, the band’s first in six years, from rehearsals to stadiums. Underneath it is the question of how long this can go on: Bruce in his seventies, a band touched by illness and loss, and a setlist built around memory and mortality.
caveat: On Hulu in the US; on Disney+ in most other countries.

title: Nebraska Live
note: Nebraska (1982) was a set of four-track home demos that Bruce chose to release as they were, and its lo-fi starkness has shaped generations of songwriters. More than forty years later he performed it in full for the first time, filmed in black and white with no audience and no talking. Quiet and haunted, best watched late at night.
also: Also to rent or buy digitally

title: Springsteen: Deliver Me From Nowhere
note: A dramatized account of the making of Nebraska, with Jeremy Allen White as Bruce and Jeremy Strong as Jon Landau. It dwells on the isolation and depression behind the record rather than the stadium years that followed. Pair it with Nebraska Live.
caveat: On Hulu in the US; on Disney+ in most other countries.

title: Philadelphia 2026
note: The finale of the 2026 Land of Hope and Dreams American Tour, filmed in full and released in parts on Bruce’s own channel. At 76 he’s still using the stage as a pulpit, with a setlist shaped to tell a story about the country. Proof that the late period is no victory lap.
